intro: This unit is about one family. The Torah says God told Abraham and Sarah to leave home. They went to a new land. Their family grew. Isaac and Rebekah came next. Then Jacob, Leah and Rachel. Then Joseph and his brothers.

Jewish tradition calls Abraham and Sarah the first of its family. Jewish families read these stories every year. In this unit we learn what the Torah says. We learn what the stories mean to the people who read them. We do not decide if they are true. We listen and we learn.

By the end, you will be able to tell how Abraham and Sarah welcomed guests. You will know Jacob's dream and his new name. You will know how Joseph forgave his brothers. And you will know how the twelve tribes got their names.
bigQuestion: What do the Torah's stories of Abraham's family say about promises, kindness and forgiving?

timeline.t: The Torah says God tells Abram and Sarai to leave home for a new land
God promises Abram a family as many as the stars
Three travelers come, and Abraham runs to feed them
Isaac is born; his name means "he laughs"
Rebekah waters ten camels at the well and marries Isaac
Twins are born: Esau and Jacob
Jacob dreams of a ladder to the sky
Jacob marries Leah and Rachel and has twelve sons and a daughter
Jacob wrestles all night and gets the name Israel
Joseph's brothers sell him, and he is taken to Egypt
Joseph becomes Pharaoh's top helper and saves food
Joseph forgives his brothers, and the family moves to Egypt

words.d: something you say you will do, and then you do it
the man the Torah says left home for a new land; Jewish tradition calls him the first of the family
a person who comes to visit your home
a story Jewish teachers tell to add to a Torah story
the son of Abraham and Sarah; his Hebrew name means "he laughs"
the new name the Torah says Jacob was given; his family became the people of Israel
a very big family group; the Torah names twelve tribes of Israel
to stop being angry at someone for what they did

test.q: What does the Torah say God told Abram to do?
choices: Leave his land for a new one
test.why: Genesis 12 says God told Abram to leave his land and go to a land God would show him.

test.q: What did Abraham do when three strangers came?
choices: He ran to give them food
test.why: Genesis 18 says Abraham ran to meet the travelers and gave them a big meal.

test.q: What does the midrash say about Abraham's tent?
choices: It was open on all sides
test.why: A midrash says Abraham's tent was open on all sides so any guest could come in.

test.q: Who were Isaac's mother and father?
test.why: Isaac was the son of Sarah and Abraham.

test.q: What did Rebekah do for the stranger's camels?
test.why: Genesis 24 says Rebekah drew water for the man and all ten of his camels.
Genesis 25 says Isaac and Rebekah had twins, Esau and Jacob.

test.q: In Jacob's dream, what went up and down the ladder?
test.why: Genesis 28 says angels were going up and down the ladder.

test.q: What new name did Jacob get?
test.why: The Torah says Jacob's new name was Israel. Beth-el is a place and Canaan is a land.

test.q: How many sons did Jacob have?
test.why: The Torah says Jacob had twelve sons, and the twelve tribes are named for them.

test.q: What did Joseph do when his brothers came to Egypt for food?
test.why: Genesis 45 says Joseph told his brothers who he was and forgave them.

write.prompt: Pick one person from this unit: Abraham (Genesis 18), Rebekah (Genesis 24), Jacob (Genesis 28) or Joseph (Genesis 45). Draw or write one kind or brave thing the Torah says they did. Then tell what Jewish tradition says we can learn from it.
tips: Say which person and story you picked, like "Abraham, Genesis 18."
Say "the Torah says" when you tell what happened.
Say "Jewish tradition says" when you tell what the story teaches.
Use two words from the unit, like guest, promise or forgive.
